title: What Fits in One Carry-On
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] I used to travel with a suitcase heavy enough to require its own small negotiation with airline staff, packed against every contingency I could plausibly imagine.
Narrator: Rain I might encounter, occasions I might be invited to, versions of myself I might suddenly need to become, all of it dutifully folded and zipped shut.
Narrator: [carefully] The turn came on a trip where the airline lost that suitcase entirely, and I spent a week wearing essentially the same three items, laundered nightly in hotel sinks.
Narrator: I expected the deprivation to feel exactly like deprivation, and was mildly startled when it began, instead, to feel something closer to relief.
Narrator: [reflective] Fewer decisions each morning, for one thing, and fewer possessions to track, worry over, or feel vaguely responsible for throughout the day.
Narrator: I noticed, too, how much of my original packing had been armour against imagined judgment, outfits assembled for versions of the trip that never actually materialised.
Narrator: [honestly] Since then, I've travelled with one carry-on regardless of the trip's length, a discipline that initially felt like deprivation and now feels closer to clarity.
Narrator: It requires a certain relinquishing, admittedly, an acceptance that I might occasionally be underdressed, occasionally re-wear something someone's already seen.
Narrator: [gently] The world, it turns out, does not particularly notice or care, which is either humbling or liberating depending on the day.
Narrator: What I've gained isn't merely lighter luggage but a kind of portable minimalism, a sense that I need considerably less than I once assumed to feel adequately myself.
Narrator: [calmly] I still occasionally miscalculate, arrive somewhere cold with nothing warm enough, and shiver through an evening I could have easily prepared for.
Narrator: But I've come to prefer the occasional shiver to the old, heavier certainty, dragged through airports, that I might need absolutely everything, just in case.
